James Stephens, The Crock of Gold.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/james-stephens/the-crock-of-gold

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- James Stephens, the author, died 1950 (Wikidata Q508101, P570 = 1950-12-26).

First publication of the text used: 1912 (SE colophon: 'The Crock of Gold was published in 1912 by James Stephens.'). The Wikipedia article says the novel was first published in 1912 and names Macmillan & Co. as publisher. It does not give the place of first publication.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1912, before 1931, so the US rule settles its origin too. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 2007.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom or Ireland; the Wikipedia article does not give the place of first publication): both use life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above (1950), so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2021.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

- Wikidata Q508101 (James Stephens), P570 = 1950-12-26
